If there is plan to get 4.1 done in near future (few months), then there is not too many points to use (time) resources for 4.0.2 release. Yes, it's the correct way, but.... 

From pen-test company perspective - with new ASVS release it requires some migration work anyway and if I can see new 4.1 release is coming, I would skip to take in use 4.0.2. I don't remember that someone wanted after ASVS 4.0 release pen-test using ASVS 3.0.1, except already fixed contracts.

@tghosth  comment from issue #666 

> The target release date for the next OWASP Top 10 is mid-Feb 2021 so I doubt we will see a 4.1 before the end of April 2021.

If due date for 4.1 is not clear or is far away then I would like to get some version/release for fixes since March 2019. Other ways all the fixes are not usable for fixing ASVS version to pen-test contract (problem described in #666).

For small changes there should be goal/plan/strategy for new releases (cycle/interval). For example, wording fixes, typos etc once per quarter?

Ok, I have created a 4.0.2 branch and I have spent some time back-porting all the "bleeding edge" changes which I believe match @vanderaj requirements above

> The only thing I would countenance here is duplicate issue removal, spelling fixes, and clarifications.

@vanderaj @jmanico  @danielcuthbert  @m8urnett  please can you take a look at the changes and let me know if you approve. We can then decide if there is anything else we want to do before we release.

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/v4.0.2

I need to agree with @ThunderSon here and I link my arguments again here - #666. From @tghosth comment https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/666#issuecomment-530967509 I assume he has pretty similar view to this topic.

This is something, where we should move. For a starter, we should get the v4.0.2 out to get some movement. 

I agree that next release in next year is not very good perspective. There are some known issues which requires restructuring, and it means this issue is/will be known more than a year before it actually get a chance to get some fix.

As I'm not anyhow officially related with OWASP or ASVS, I don't know what kind of resource issues here may exists or why those milestones are like they are.

My proposal is - let's get this v4.0.2 out first. This is just a "small fixes release" and can be clearly written to the document.

All this release plan and ideology is must have, like I wrote already in #666, but please, AFTER v4.0.2 is out. At the moment it is really confusing - do we get this v4.0.2 out at all or we start again and again the same discussion ([now in Twitter](https://twitter.com/dcuthbert/status/1277169753954701314)), should we release v4.0.2, or v4.1 or v5.0 etc. It's a bit demotivating to put effort into project if declared plans may change or dropped in last minute. If there is direction and the path declared and said out, please follow it (if there are no clear and huge reasons to choose other direction).

(From Twitter discussion) Personally, I don't watch v4.0.2 and v4.1 as parallel standards - there is no v4.1 yet, there is just bleeding edge, which will be v4.1. Till it's not done, there is only v4.0.2 (if it will be released) as only stable release to reference. Like at the moment there is v4.0.1.
